items.title: Make the boot screen communicate actual download progress
items.what: On the ShoeMoney loading screen, the rail beneath “Downloading the game” appears almost entirely dark with no visible percentage, downloaded size, phase, or activity beyond the static message.
items.why: A player waiting on a mobile WebGPU download cannot tell whether loading is progressing or stalled, increasing abandonment before the first bout.
items.how: Fill the rail from the real asset-loader ratio, add text such as “42% · 18 MB / 43 MB,” rotate the phase label through “Preparing arena,” “Loading fighters,” and “Compiling shaders,” and show a retry control if progress has not changed for several seconds.

items.title: Remove ambiguity from the two-stick instructions
items.what: In the lower gameplay legend, STANCE labels both horizontal directions as “step” — “◀ step” and “▶ step” — while the technique stick uses “back / forward.” The move list also relies on tiny circular direction icons that are not immediately self-explanatory.
items.why: A first-time phone player cannot tell what the two horizontal stance inputs do or how a visible stick gesture becomes a named attack, causing missed inputs and unnecessary opening the Moves panel.
items.how: Change the legend to explicit labels such as “step left / step right” or “retreat / advance,” add a one-line first-use prompt showing “hold stance direction + technique direction,” and display a larger gesture diagram for the currently selected move.

items.title: Give the wide viewport a real gameplay layout
items.what: In the landscape screenshot, the dojo occupies only the upper portion of the screen, the fighters and playfield are relatively small, and a large unused black area sits below them; the stance and technique sticks are reduced to tiny controls at the far left and right edges.
items.why: The wide layout wastes screen space and makes touch controls harder to hit, while the player loses the cinematic scale and immediate readability present in portrait.
items.how: Add a landscape breakpoint that expands the playfield vertically into the unused lower region, places the two sticks in a dedicated bottom control band, and scales each stick to a minimum touch diameter of roughly 120–140 CSS pixels.

items.title: Turn the Moves sheet into a usable phone reference
items.what: The TECHNIQUES panel is a dense full-height list; at the bottom of the shown screen, “Rising Knee” is followed by a partially cut-off next row with no obvious scrollbar, tab structure, or indication that more moves continue below.
items.why: Players trying to learn combinations cannot reliably see the complete move set or know whether the panel is scrollable, forcing trial and error during a timed bout.
items.how: Group moves into compact Forward, Back, Up, and Down sections with collapsible headers, reserve safe-area padding below the last row, add a visible scroll cue, and keep each move row to a clear input graphic, name, and scoring result.

items.title: Explain the unlabeled gold number in the match HUD
items.what: During gameplay, the top HUD shows a gold “30,” then “29,” in the center between the fighters’ scores, but the number has no TIME label, clock icon, or unit; it visually resembles another score.
items.why: Point-karate decisions depend on knowing how much time remains, and an unlabeled changing number makes the most urgent match state slower to parse on a small screen.
items.how: Add a compact “TIME” caption or clock icon above the number, keep the seconds visually distinct from both scores, and apply a clear final-five-seconds state such as a restrained pulse or color shift without changing the warm dojo palette.
